questions.question: In what order does Python search scopes when resolving a name (the LEGB rule)?
questions.explanation: Python checks Local, then Enclosing function scopes, then the module Global scope, then Built-ins, stopping at the first match.

questions.question: Why does `print(count)` raise UnboundLocalError in a function that later does `count = 1`, even though a global `count` exists?
options: Global variables cannot be read inside functions
Any assignment in the function body makes the name local for the whole function, decided at compile time
The global variable is deleted when the function is called
questions.explanation: Scope is determined at compile time; because count is assigned in the body, it is local throughout, so reading it before assignment fails.

questions.question: Given `def transfer(src, dst, /, amount, *, currency="INR")`, which call is valid?
questions.explanation: src and dst are positional-only, amount can be passed either way, and currency is keyword-only after the bare `*`.

questions.question: Why does `def add_tag(tag, tags=[])` return a growing list across separate calls?
options: Lists are copied on every call but the copy is cached
Python reuses the last return value automatically
append() modifies a global list named tags
The default list is created once when `def` runs and the same object is reused on every call
questions.explanation: Defaults are evaluated once at definition time; use `tags=None` and create a new list inside the function instead.
